# sipnab

> SIP and RTP capture, analysis and diagnosis. One static binary that reads live traffic, a pcap, or a HEP feed, and reports call flow, RTP quality, NAT and security findings.

This file indexes the documentation as plain text. `llms-full.txt` beside it carries every page concatenated.

## Docs

- [Use sipnab as a Rust library](https://sipnab.com/docs/library/): Use the Rust parser and analysis types from an external application.
- [Run the example Python clients](https://sipnab.com/docs/examples/): Run Python clients for correlation, MCP queries and vCon inspection, with local regression tests.
- [Recipes for common tasks](https://sipnab.com/docs/cookbook/): Worked examples with real output: triage, filtering, HEP, TLS decryption, MCP, observability, security and audio export, each one a command you can paste and the result it produces.
- [Scrape Prometheus metrics](https://sipnab.com/docs/metrics/): Every metric family sipnab emits, what each one means, which are counters and which are gauges, and the scrape config. Split out of the REST API page, which a scrape target's reader never needs.
- [Query the REST API](https://sipnab.com/docs/api/): sipnab's REST API: authentication, every endpoint with its response shape, status codes, curl recipes, and the security model. Metric names and their meaning are on the Prometheus metrics page.
- [Connect an AI agent (MCP)](https://sipnab.com/docs/mcp/): Drive sipnab from an AI agent over the Model Context Protocol: what it is, a first working example, and where to go for deployment, the tool reference, and the protocol contract.
- [Install sipnab](https://sipnab.com/docs/install/): Install sipnab from a pre-built binary, a package, Homebrew or cargo, then check the download is genuine.
- [Name calls on an rtpengine relay](https://sipnab.com/docs/rtpengine/): Media captured on a standalone rtpengine relay comes back orphaned because a relay carries no SIP. Read rtpengine's own control plane to name the calls, with no change to an existing Homer pipeline.
- [Troubleshoot a call](https://sipnab.com/docs/troubleshooting/): Start from what the caller reports, find the matching section, and run the commands it gives, in order.
- [Walk through the terminal UI](https://sipnab.com/docs/tui/): Your first analysis in the interactive TUI, step by step: open a capture, read the ladder, measure a delay, and inspect RTP.
- [Look up a key binding](https://sipnab.com/docs/keybindings/): Complete TUI keyboard shortcut reference for all views.
- [Change the terminal UI colors](https://sipnab.com/docs/theme/): Customize sipnab's TUI colors with 11 semantic color slots and preset themes.
- [Look up a command-line flag](https://sipnab.com/docs/cli/): Every flag sipnab takes, grouped by job: capture, matching, output, analysis, security, the listeners and MCP.
- [Filter calls and streams](https://sipnab.com/docs/filter-dsl/): Declarative filter language for matching SIP dialogs and RTP streams.
- [Look up a SIP header field](https://sipnab.com/docs/sip-header-fields/): Every SIP header field in the IANA registry, its compact form, and the RFC that defines it.
- [Look up a SIP method](https://sipnab.com/docs/sip-methods/): Every SIP method in the IANA registry, the RFC section defining it, and which dialog state machine sipnab runs it through.
- [Look up a SIP parameter](https://sipnab.com/docs/sip-parameters/): Every SIP URI parameter, header-field parameter and option tag in the IANA registry, with the RFC that defines it.
- [Understand MOS and codecs](https://sipnab.com/docs/mos-and-codecs/): Where the quality score comes from, which codecs have a published impairment factor behind it, and which report a placeholder.
- [Look up a SIP response code](https://sipnab.com/docs/sip-response-codes/): Every SIP response code in the IANA registry, the RFC section that defines it, and whether it means the call failed.
- [Choose an output format](https://sipnab.com/docs/output-formats/): Machine-readable output: NDJSON, summary reports, dialog/stream JSON, and pcap/pcapng.
- [Configure sipnab](https://sipnab.com/docs/config/): TOML configuration file format and all configurable sections.
- [Read TLS without keys (eBPF)](https://sipnab.com/docs/uprobe-walkthrough/): What uprobe and eBPF capture is and is NOT, its security implications, whether your kernel supports it at all, and how to run both backends step by step.
- [Deploy the MCP server](https://sipnab.com/docs/mcp-deploy/): Step-by-step MCP deployment scenarios: same-box stdio, remote production servers over SSH or HTTP, HEP capture hosts, TLS endpoints, fleets, and headless automation.
- [Use MCP across many servers](https://sipnab.com/docs/mcp-estate/): Several SIP servers feeding one capture host, reaching sipnab from outside the network, one agent holding many capture hosts, and following one call across an SBC, a proxy and a PBX.
- [Look up an MCP tool](https://sipnab.com/docs/mcp-tools/): Every MCP tool sipnab exposes, what question each answers, and the fields it returns.
- [Check the MCP protocol contract](https://sipnab.com/docs/mcp-protocol/): The MCP wire contract: security model, what the write verbs may do, untrusted capture text, the stdio invariant, and error semantics.
- [Look up a SIP conformance rule](https://sipnab.com/docs/sip-lint-rules/): Every rule the SIP conformance linter runs, the RFC section behind it, the severity and basis it reports under, and how to suppress it in CI.
- [Stop a capture dropping packets](https://sipnab.com/docs/tuning-capture/): Size the kernel capture ring, read the kernel and interface drop counters, tell the two apart, and decide between the any device and a named interface.
- [Build a vCon capture stack](https://sipnab.com/docs/vcon-harness/): Build a two-point vCon capture stack (OpenSIPS, rtpengine, sipnab and a conserver), then operate it, verify a stored call carries its media, and recognize the failures that look like success.
- [Export a call as a vCon](https://sipnab.com/docs/vcon/): Export one observed dialog as a vCon container: what the format is, how to produce one, and what an observer's record does and does not let a consumer conclude.
- [Read SIP inside tunnels](https://sipnab.com/docs/encapsulations/): Which link types, EtherTypes and tunnels sipnab can read a SIP dialog out of, which it cannot, and what it reports when a frame does not decode.
- [Learn from real captures](https://sipnab.com/docs/real-world-captures/): Twelve findings read out of live carrier and PBX traffic, with the command, the output and what an operator does next: the retransmit storms, false-positive detections and misleading aggregates that a curated fixture cannot show.
- [Triage a capture from the command line](https://sipnab.com/docs/first-cli-triage/): A first analysis without the TUI: list the calls in a capture, find the ones that went wrong, explain one, and hand the answer to another tool as JSON.
- [Glossary](https://sipnab.com/docs/glossary/): The VoIP and sipnab terms the other pages use, each defined in one short entry by what it means in sipnab's output.
- [Authenticate API and MCP clients](https://sipnab.com/docs/auth/): Bearer-token authentication for the REST API and MCP server: token format, audience binding, configuring a signing key, minting tokens, expiry and key rotation.

## Internals

- [Domain Primer](https://sipnab.com/docs/internals/domain-primer/): The SIP and RTP model the code assumes you already have — written for the Rust engineer who is new to VoIP.
- [Subsystem Guide](https://sipnab.com/docs/internals/subsystem-guide/): One packet's journey from the wire to the screen, traced function by function across all four packet paths.
- [Invariants](https://sipnab.com/docs/internals/invariants/): The rules that must not break: what each one is, why it exists, what enforces it, and how it fails when broken.
- [Test Architecture](https://sipnab.com/docs/internals/testing/): The test tiers, what each one asserts, how to regenerate its fixtures, and the self-enforcing gate tests.
- [Contributor Walkthroughs](https://sipnab.com/docs/internals/walkthroughs/): Ordered checklists for the changes people actually make: a new TUI view, a new detector, a new CLI flag, a new MCP tool.
- [Build, CI and Release](https://sipnab.com/docs/internals/build-ci-release/): What compiles, what gates a merge, what runs on a tag, and which of those you can safely ignore.
- [Threading Model](https://sipnab.com/docs/internals/threading/): Thread topology, the channels between them, and the lock discipline that keeps the synchronous packet path synchronous.
- [Zero-Copy Payloads](https://sipnab.com/docs/internals/zero-copy-payloads/): The bytes::Bytes spine from capture to output — including a performance claim the page itself refutes.
- [TUI Testing](https://sipnab.com/docs/internals/tui-testing/): Snapshot, state and interaction testing for the terminal UI.
- [Profiling](https://sipnab.com/docs/internals/profiling/): Where sipnab's time actually goes, and how to find out on this hardware without guessing.
- [The rtpengine Control Plane](https://sipnab.com/docs/internals/rtpengine-control-plane/): Naming media captured on a standalone relay: the ng wire format, why the Call-ID arrives over HEP, and how a paired capture proves it.
- [Relay Control Decoding](https://sipnab.com/docs/internals/relay-control-decoding/): Reading rtpengine's ng and rtpproxy's text control planes behind one seam: why direction decides, what neither protocol carries, and the bounds a sniffed datagram meets.
- [Uprobe TLS Capture](https://sipnab.com/docs/internals/uprobe-capture/): Reading SIP plaintext out of a process's TLS library with kernel uprobes, and why each step refuses rather than guesses.
- [The vCon Exporter](https://sipnab.com/docs/internals/vcon/): Where each vCon section comes from, the completeness caveat carried in two surfaces from one value, and the deterministic uuid.
